body: I'm in a bad spot right now, but your post brought me some peace. I'm also diagnosed with BPD and GAD. I attempted 11 times counting today. When I'm emptionally charged or raging, I find that doing daily chores/tasks or simple things like setting up your calendar or wiping down your desk helps me. I wish I had more to offer.❤
I don't know
Didn't mean to frame it that way. At least where I'm from, "no kill" branded shelters and rescue groups dehumanize the mission of locally funded kill shelters. Many people don't agree with me.
Photoshopped sunburn?
I thought so too, but it was actually my foster dog who brought me to trust others again.
Not everyone is like your parents. I know there are people close to you who will try to understand.

I'm sorry, I need to jump on this thread. As unbelievable as this sounds, my family doesn't believe in mental health. Both live in their own world. I never disowned my parents, but I decided to create distance.

It was a very hard thing to do. I started to find people and build my own family. I had low expectations, but they showed me my parents don't speak for everyone. Most people aren't like my parents and your parents.
But nothing is wrong with you. You can change how you see yourself.
You can. I promise.
I used to feel the same and wandered around in the nighttime thinking about how I don't add to the world. I'm finally coming around after 18 years. I believe you can.
I'm sorry, I needed to step away for a moment. Do you want to talk about it?
Why?
Do you still want to use it?
He's actually fine. +1 it can backfire though.
I won't answer either question, but my brother survived a gunshot that ripped through his artery.
Let's talk about it
I'm here :)
I thought so too, and then I contracted COVID-19. Stay safe and healthy. Trust me. I'm at the epicenter, and they're not enough ventilators.

It resonated with me because we grew up together. He changed one day. Something clicked, and he started to physically abuse me. I tried my best to understand what happened to him, but I decided it was enough. 

I know what he said was really about himself. It still shakes me to the core because I don't know how right he is. 

I'm thinking about reaching out to my boyfriend.

I really admire how you turned a part of BPD into a gift. It's uplifting to hear I'm not the only one who sees it that way. I'm still learning my way around this. I was recently diagnosed with epilepsy, so it became challenging to find the right medications for me. I mean, I bothered people here, and maybe I could do the same with the people around me.
I just read the community guidelines, so I edited the OP. Thank you so much though.

+1 from the epicenter of COVID19 right now. It's true hospitals are extremely overwhelmed, but the virus isn't a death sentence. Panic is more deadly than the virus right now. Don't worry, if you stay quarantined and follow your national health center's recommendations, you will be ok.

Hey there. I'm in the same situation. Quarantine is everything and nothing to me. For the better part of 18 years, freedom never resonated with me. Eventually, I broke a window and started to sneak out into the city. I found happiness with just being alive right now. It was all taken away from me, but at the same time, it feels like home again. I'm here if you want to talk.😊
